recipes.name: Pumpkin Chipotle Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, minced

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour; cook until golden brown, about 3 minutes. Whisk in vegetable stock; bring to a boil over high heat. Whisk in pumpkin purée until no lumps remain, then stir in half-and-half, chipotle peppers, sofrito, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and paprika. Return to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low; cook until thickened and hot, about 8 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Chipotle Soup
raw_recipe.description: This quick pumpkin chipotle soup recipe uses pumpkin purée, half-and-half, canned chipotles in adobo sauce, sofrito, Worcestershire sauce, and paprika.

review.reviewBody: I have made this soup at least 20 times in the past couple of years, and have tweaked it a bit....I like to dice an onion and saute in a TBSP of light butter until soft. I use almond milk in place of a the cream, and chipotle seasoning powder in place of the adobo. I also like mine very spicy, so I add lots of cayenne and fresh ground black pepper. The perfect topping for this is a TBSP sour cream (I use fat-free) or a dollop of goat cheese. I eat this several times a week in the winter; with the above modifications, it's actually a very low-calorie soup.

Love this soup! I also sauté onion in the butter before adding a bit of garlic then the addition of the flour. Added the stock and followed the recipe. At the end I like to add cooked shrimp, cilantro, sour cream and avocado. So good!

Here are my changes based on the reviews: I put an onion, two cloves of garlic and the peppers in my food processor and finely chopped them up. I sauteed the mixture in butter and then added the flour and broth. I cut the paprika to 1/4 tsp and used "smoked paprika" instead. I also cut the worchestire sauce to 1/4 teaspoon (we are not too fond of it). I added a 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon and a small grating of nutmeg. It is delicious but next time I would use homemade sofrito; the Goya stuff was kinda funky. One of my kids thought it was too spicy.

I've made this several times and this last tweak was the best yet. Forget all that butter and cream! Like others, I used non-fat canned milk. I sauteed a small, finely chopped onion to dark golden, then used used 2-Tablespoons of olive oil to make my roux with the flour and broth (organic veggie broth). I also used 1.5-teaspoons of both ground chipolte powder and smoky paprika (to taste). I was in a hurry and did not make sofrito, but added 1/4-cup chopped cilantro and 1-teaspoon finely minced garlic. If you want a completely creamy version, blend it. We like the slight texture.
Wanted to recommend using the sofrito in the freezer section over the jarred variety in the Hispanic section.

This is a good start to a great soup! Without the added additions I found it to be a bit bland. I sautéed an onion before adding the flour, and after adding all ingredients I also added garlic, salt and pepper, extra chipotle pepper, and extra adobo peppers, cayenne, some brown sugar, cinnamon and a hint of nutmeg, and I also added extra With these changes, you will have the most delicious Chipotle Pumpkin Soup! (I like the heat so decrease the amount of chipotle, adobo peppers, and cayenne and it still tastes great!)

I made this with recommendations from other posters in mind-- I subbed half chicken broth/half vegetable broth because that is what I had, and added a small minced onion and 2 cloves minced garlic to the initial step. I also used half cream and half 2% milk. I agreed with reviewers that thought it a bit bland (spicy, but still a flat flavor) and I added 1/4 tsp of ground cumin, 2 tsp of garlic salt (instead of salt), and 1 tablespoon blackstrap molasses. The last addition was inspired by one reviewer who speculated maple syrup would help, and another who added brown sugar to great success. I think the cumin is what assisted the middle flavors, but the molasses unified all the elements together.

Yum-azing! My first go at any kind of pumpkin soup, and it turned out delish!

I like spice, so I used 4 of the chipotle peppers with some of the sauce, and a few dashes of chili powder..still not overpowering, as I added a bit of brown sugar as well. I also used the evaporated milk instead of the half & half as others have suggested, added nutmeg, and made sautéed onions and garlic instead of the sofrito. 

Can't wait to top it off with some avocado, cilantro, and perhaps a dollop of sour cream tonight for dinner!

I didn't have vegetable stock or sofrito so I used chicken stock and 2 tbsn of cilantro flakes instead.
I've never been a big fan of pumpkin, but my 13 yr old loves everything pumpkin. So, I made it for him.
It was surprisingly delicious and simple to make. We'll be making this often. 
Love it!

This was absolutely delicious. I did "make it my own" based on some previous reviews- started with onion and garlic sautéed in the butter then added cumin and garam masala to the paprika. Only added about 3/4 cut half and half. I served it with pipitas, avacado and cilantro. I will definitely make again and serve with warm cornbread!

This recipe was so good.... once I doubled the Chipotle, paprika and sofrito. I also added about a tablespoon of cayenne pepper. Now to be true to the recipe, I sampled the original recipe made as written before making any changes. It tastes like watery pumpkin and needs more oomph. Fantastic once pepped up a bit.

Make sure you have the right amount of pumpkin, I saw one can and assumed it was the normal 15 oz one, not double! Very tasty though I wouldn’t call it spicy, added in a bunch of cayenne to kick it up
This soup is amazing, and it's so easy to make. My husband declared it phenomenal!

We've made this soup numerous times. My family loves it. My son requests it as part of his birthday meal. Add an extra chipotle, a dash of cumin, and a pinch of cinnamon. We look forward to this soup as often as we can.

I sauteed onions before adding the flour, and I let it all simmer for about a half hour, to get things all cohesive. I used fresh pumpkin and it was almost the entire pie pumpkin to equal a 29 ounce can. Is a tangy soup, I may eliminate some Worcestershire or sofritos next time.
It was good but I kind of got it too hot. Nice simple pumpkin soup recipe, just watch the heat!
I loved it as written but added a flourish or two such as grated ginger and a little chopped candied ginger (love ginger) Also some chopped onion and garlic. Hope additions count in overall rating.

I used chicken stock , heavy cream and cornstarch instead of veggie broth, half and half, and flour. 

Soup was AMAZING!!

I did make a few changes that only made it better. I only used one chipotle pepper because more makes it too spicy for me to enjoy. I used fat free half and half. I often use that in cooking to help with calorie count. I also used smoked paprika. I loved the warmth of flavor that adds. This soup turned out great and is now one of my favorites.
